subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
intro: Gravity is a force of attraction between any two objects that have mass. Gravitational force is always attractive (it pulls objects together, never pushes them apart). The strength of gravity depends on the masses of the objects: the more mass, the stronger the pull. That is why objects fall toward Earth, Earth has enormous mass. Gravity also depends on distance, but the key idea here is that gravity is attractive and depends on mass. The Sun's huge mass keeps the planets in orbit.

items.prompt: Is the gravitational force between the Earth and the Moon attractive or repulsive?

steps: Gravity is always a force of attraction between objects with mass.
The Earth and Moon both have mass.
So the gravitational force between them is attractive.
solution.answer: Attractive; gravity always pulls objects together.

items.prompt: Why is the Sun able to hold the planets in orbit?

steps: Gravitational force is stronger when objects have more mass.
The Sun has an enormous mass.
Its strong gravity pulls on the planets and keeps them in orbit.
solution.answer: Because the Sun's huge mass creates a strong gravitational pull on the planets.

items.prompt: Planet A has more mass than Planet B. Which exerts a stronger gravitational pull on a nearby moon of the same distance?

steps: Gravity depends on the mass of the objects.
Planet A has more mass than Planet B.
So Planet A exerts a stronger gravitational pull.
solution.answer: Planet A, because it has more mass.

items.prompt: Is gravity attractive, repulsive, or both?

steps: Gravity is always attractive; it pulls objects together.

items.prompt: What property of objects does the strength of gravity depend on?

steps: The strength of gravity depends on the masses of the objects.

items.prompt: Why do objects fall toward the Earth?

steps: Earth's large mass creates a gravitational pull that attracts objects toward it.
solution.answer: Because Earth's large mass pulls them toward it.
